subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the condition for the lines joining the origin to the points of intersection of the circle x²+y²=a² and the line lx+my=1 to coincide.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what coincident means as a condition on the pair.

steps.label: Write the chord and the circle
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. The chord is already given as lx + my = 1 — exactly the '= 1' form homogenisation needs — so no clearing is required here, unlike the earlier questions in the run.
lines: Given circle is  x² + y² = a²  ⇒  x² + y² − a² = 0  ……(2)

recall.must_convey: That the chord lx + my = 1 and the circle x² + y² − a² = 0 are written down.
accept: write the chord and the circle, the chord is already equal to one
l x plus m y equals one is already in the right form
the circle is x squared plus y squared minus a squared equals zero
chord already equals one form lo undi
note the chord and the circle

steps.why: Homogenisation needs the line as (something) = 1, and this question hands it over that way — which is why the whole answer is shorter than its neighbours.
common_mistakes: Rearranging the chord unnecessarily and introducing a sign error.
Leaving the circle as x² + y² = a² and forgetting to move a² across.
steps.memory_tip: The chord already reads = 1, exactly the form homogenisation needs — no clearing required.

steps.label: Homogenise the circle
steps.margin_note: First mark. The circle has no linear term at all, so only the constant needs raising — multiply −a² by (lx + my)², the chord squared.

recall.must_convey: That the constant −a² is multiplied by (lx + my)², the chord squared.
accept: multiply the constant by the chord squared
the circle has no linear term so only a squared is homogenised
replace one by l x plus m y and square it
constant ki chord square multiply cheyyali
homogenise the circle with the chord

steps.why: A circle centred at the origin has no linear term, so homogenisation touches only its constant — the simplest case of the method.
common_mistakes: Multiplying the x² and y² terms by the chord as well.
Multiplying the constant by the chord only once.
steps.memory_tip: The circle has no linear term, so only the CONSTANT needs raising: multiply −a² by the chord squared.

steps.label: Collect the coefficients
steps.margin_note: One mark. Expand the square and group by x², y² and xy. Each coefficient carries an a² and the letters l and m, which is what the closing condition will compare.

recall.must_convey: That expanding gives x²(1 − a²l²) + y²(1 − a²m²) − 2a²lm·xy = 0.
accept: expand the chord squared and collect the three coefficients
group into x squared y squared and x y terms
one minus a squared l squared is the x squared coefficient
expand chesi coefficients collect cheyyali
write it as a pair of lines through the origin
heard_as: one minus a squared l squared

steps.why: Naming the three coefficients explicitly is what makes the closing condition a one-line substitution rather than another expansion.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the 2 in the 2lmxy cross term.
Dropping a² from one of the three coefficients.
steps.memory_tip: Expand and group by x², y² and xy. Each coefficient carries an a² and the letters l, m.

steps.label: Apply the coincident condition
steps.margin_note: The last two marks — one for stating h² = ab, one for carrying it through. Coincident means the two lines are the SAME line, which for a pair is exactly h² = ab.
lines: Write the pair's coefficients as A, B, H, because the letter a is already the circle's radius here.
If this pair of lines are coincident then  H² = AB
Here A = (1 − a²l²), B = (1 − a²m²), 2H = −2a²lm ⇒ H = −a²lm

recall.must_convey: That coincident lines satisfy h² = ab, which reduces to a²l² + a²m² = 1.
accept: coincident means h squared equals a b
the two lines are the same so the discriminant condition is h squared equals a b
the a to the fourth terms cancel leaving a squared l squared plus a squared m squared equals one
coincident ayithe h square equals a b
apply h squared equals a b and simplify

steps.why: h² − ab measures how far apart the two lines of the pair are: positive means two distinct lines, zero means they have merged into one. So coincident is exactly h² = ab.
common_mistakes: Using h² > ab, which is the condition for two DISTINCT lines.
Forgetting that both sides carry a⁴l²m², so it cancels.
steps.memory_tip: Coincident lines mean h² = ab — the equal-roots condition for the pair.

insider_note: Homogenise by replacing the constant a² with a²(lx + my)², then apply h² = ab, because coincident lines are the equal-root case. The a⁴l²m² cancels on both sides, leaving a²(l² + m²) = 1.
